name: 03-small-world-rewiring
title: Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring
question: How does random rewiring of a ring lattice change its structure?
hypothesis: Rewiring a small fraction of lattice edges collapses path length while clustering stays high — the small-world regime — without changing node or edge counts.
objective: Run the small_world_rewire reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `small_world_rewire` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

config.title: Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring
config.subtitle: a ring lattice dissolves into a small world as random rewires accumulate

expected_behavior.name: sw-conserves-edges
expected_behavior.condition: edge count is unchanged throughout (rewiring, not growth)
expected_behavior.rationale: Each rewire moves one endpoint; it never adds or removes an edge.

expected_behavior.name: sw-shortcuts
expected_behavior.condition: mean degree conserved while long-range shortcuts appear
expected_behavior.rationale: Rewiring conserves total degree but introduces cross-ring shortcuts.

behavior_tests.name: sw-edge-count-conserved
behavior_tests.description: Edge count equals the initial ring-lattice edge count at the end.

findings.name: small_world_rewire-signature
findings.summary: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.
findings.detail: Edge and node counts stay fixed while rewired shortcuts cross the ring — the hallmark of the Watts–Strogatz construction. The circular layout makes each rewire visible as a chord.
